texts: On the night of day 111 of Year 1, Bevin Coombe was ill.
Halden tended the Stilllight Lantern that night in place of Bevin Coombe.
Halden refilled the mire-essence of the Stilllight Lantern at midnight.
The wick of the Stilllight Lantern was carbonized.
Halden did not trim the wick.
The Stilllight Lantern burned dim for three hours.
The Stilllight Lantern gave weak mist-light for three hours.
The Council judged that the dim burning was equivalent to an untended night.

q1_issues.issue: The sealed complement of "judged that the dim burning was equivalent..." carries no tense atom at all, but sequence of tense keeps a past-tense verb's (Past ...) inside the seal, so the reified equivalent-state and its flat half should be past-marked.

"burned dim" is encoded as a class atom on the burn event itself, whereas the instruction set routes a bare adjectival secondary predicate as a depictive concurrent state on the subject ("arrived tired") or as a Manner atom, not as a Member atom on the event witness.

q2_gaps: A day-of-year date in a non-Gregorian calendar ("day 111 of Year 1"): the (Day <n>) term is specified as the day-of-month of a calendar date, and no convention is given for an ordinal day-of-year with no month, so (Day 111) is indistinguishable downstream from a day-of-month reading.

An adjective that is simultaneously a symmetric predicate and takes a PP complement ("was equivalent to an untended night"): the adjective's-PP-complement reification rule and the symmetric-predicate rule (which explicitly names "is equal to") both claim it, with no tie-break, and there is no guidance on whether a (Symmetric ...) tag may sit inside a seal.
review.notes: Coreference (the lantern, the wick, "the dim burning"), the "that night" term-propagation, the in-place-of Beneficiary, and the did-not-trim denial bundle are all handled per the instruction set. Whether the surface-fused agent-nominalization compound substitute_keeper should also carry (Inheritance substitute_keeper (can keep)) is arguable under the fixed-firing rule.

issues.reason: Sequence of tense is surface-mechanical — a past-tense verb inside a sealed complement keeps its (Past ...) inside the seal — so "was equivalent" must carry (Past sk_equivalent_1) plus the past-wrapped flat half inside the sealed (And ...), exactly as the parse itself wraps "Bevin Coombe was ill" at top level.

(Member sk_burn_1 dim) is true of the passage's own words (its last sentence calls it "the dim burning") and well-typed (a minted event witness is an individual, so a property attaches by Member), while the depictive rule cited covers subject-oriented states ("arrived tired") and Manner admits only manner adverbs — an eventuality-characterizing bare adjective is uncovered ground, where a true, well-typed improvisation is acceptable.

gaps_confirmed: A day-of-year ordinal with no month ("day 111 of Year 1"): (Day <n>) is specified only as a calendar date's day-of-month, so the two readings are indistinguishable downstream.

"Was equivalent to an untended night" is claimed by both the adjective's-PP-complement reification rule and the symmetric-predicate rule (which names "is equal to"), with no tie-break, and nothing states whether a (Symmetric ...) tag may sit inside a seal or must project out of one.
new_gaps: A bare adjectival secondary predicate that characterizes the EVENTUALITY rather than the subject ("the lantern burned dim", "the stars shone bright") has no named carrier: the depictive rule predicates the state of the subject, Manner takes only manner adverbs (and never a bare adjective), and nothing licenses or bars a property atom on the event witness — a licensed form would need to say which bearer, event or subject, a bare adjectival adjunct attaches to.

"at midnight" has no stated convention: the day-part constant list names dawn / noon / dusk / night but not midnight, leaving (Hour 0) and a bare `midnight` constant both defensible — precisely the optional-form split the instruction set elsewhere forbids.

Whether the agent-nominalization capability fires on a modifier+agent-noun compound fused from the surface ("a substitute Keeper" -> (Inheritance substitute_keeper (can keep))) is undetermined: both firing licences ("a symbol you fused from the surface" and "the copular predicate of the clause") appear to apply, while the rule's examples are object-incorporating nominalizations (egg_layer, dam_builder), so a rule declared "fixed, not a judgment call" is a judgment call here.
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form for the judged complement keeps the complement clause's own past tense inside the seal — (Past sk_equivalent_1) as a conjunct of the sealed (And ...) and the dual-emit flat half as (Past (Member sk_burn_1 equivalent)) inside it — with the rest of the parse unchanged.
adjudication.notes: Everything else checks out against the instruction set: the "that night" term propagation, in-place-of as Beneficiary, the stated PartOf on the wick, the did-not-trim denial bundle, and "the dim burning" resolving to the burn event witness. The one confirmed defect is narrow and does have a licensed compliant form.
